With \(C=0\), the geometric auxiliary sequence and reversed-branch sum give \(q_*=(\sqrt{17}-3)/4\) and \(t_*=(11+3\sqrt{17})/4\). With \(a=\phi_0=1\), \(\tau=100\), and every \(0<C\le1/2\), \(\phi_1<-17/3\), \(r_j<10^{-j}\), and all later positive movements total less than \(5/3\); thus \(\phi_n<-4\) at every positive index. The exact ODE converges to zero, whereas its discrete state approaches a nonzero limit. Decimal checks succeeded; the infinite claim follows from the analytic induction.

value.rationale: This is a substantive long-time fidelity test of the source's explicitly defined unconditional-positive-root, modified-energy-stable method. Even the strongly convex physical energy \(E(\phi)=\phi^2/2\) can converge to a value above \(8\), rather than its unique-minimum value zero, while the positive auxiliary decays. The exact unshifted threshold explains the mechanism, and the strict interval \(0<C\le1/2\) rules out the zero-radicand artifact. This delimits what unconditional modified-energy stability alone guarantees.
